speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I see you're experiencing double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness. To understand the scope of your symptoms, does the double vision happen in one eye or both when you look straight ahead?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: The pattern of symptoms worsening with activity and improving with rest, along with vertical diplopia, is highly suggestive of a neuromuscular junction disorder. Does your double vision ever go away completely when you close one eye?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that clarification; the absence of recent infections makes an infectious etiology less likely. Given your symmetrical weakness and diplopia that worsens with fatigue, I need to assess your muscle strength more precisely. Please rate your ability to lift your arms against resistance and push yourself up from a chair on a scale of 1 to 10.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had trouble swallowing or slurred speech. I also have not noticed breathing difficulty, and the symptoms started gradually about a month ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The absence of bulbar symptoms (swallowing/speech) and respiratory issues is reassuring; however, given the progressive onset, vertical diplopia, and fatigable weakness, I need to confirm if you experience worsening eye pain or double vision upon sustained upward gaze.

REQUEST TEST: Electromyography (EMG) and Repetitive Nerve Stimulation (RNS)
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Cranial_Nerves

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis

The normal EMG and repetitive nerve stimulation results are unexpected given your classic symptoms of fatigable weakness and vertical diplopia. To confirm the diagnosis, I need to know if you have experienced any improvement in your symptoms after taking anticholinesterase medications like pyridostigmine, and have you noticed any drooping of your eyelids?
